title: 11 links that explain today's other big drops: CG Oncology -9.4% on adowngrade, Nike -7.1% after Investor Day. Overreaction or the start ofsomething?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
The selling didn't stop at software. CG Oncology slid 9.4% after an  
RBC downgrade, Nike fell 7.1% after its first Investor Day since 2017,  
and IonQ dropped 6.5% as quantum names cooled. A couple of these fell  
with no news at all. Can you guess which?  
  
Here is the rundown, drawn from today's write-ups.  
  
\*\*1. CG Oncology (CGON)\*\* — CG Oncology shares fell -9.41% to $76.80  
from Monday's close of $84.78, with the decline unfolding during  
Tuesday's regular session after a lower open at $82.97. The pullback  
followed an RBC Capital downgrade to Sector Perform from Outperform,  
with the price target lifted only to $97 from $80, a note that flagged  
uncertainty over the regulatory path just one session after the  
PIVOT-006 data rally.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-cg-oncology-cgon-stock-down-9-88-today-39893/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-cg-oncology-cgon-stock-down-9-88-today-39893/)  
  
\*\*2. Nike (NKE)\*\* — Nike fell -7.11% to $35.54 from Monday's close of  
$38.26, a decline that unfolded during the regular session after  
shares opened at $40.20 and touched $40.68. The drop followed the  
company's first Investor Day since 2017, where the "Full Stride Ahead"  
plan was read as aggressive and back-weighted; management also flagged  
a modest fiscal 2028 EPS decline.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-nike-nke-stock-down-7-21-today-39916/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-nike-nke-stock-down-7-21-today-39916/)  
  
\*\*3. IonQ (IONQ)\*\* — IonQ slid from Monday's close of $26.45 to $24.73  
on Tuesday, a -6.50% move that unfolded during regular trading hours  
after modest premarket gains faded. The decline was sector-driven  
rather than company-specific: quantum and AI-adjacent speculative  
names extended a multi-session liquidation ahead of Nvidia's quarterly  
report, with unease over Nvidia's abrupt CEO transition keeping risk  
appetite weak.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-ionq-ionq-stock-down-6-69-today-39888/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-ionq-ionq-stock-down-6-69-today-39888/)  
  
\*\*4. Nextpower (NXT)\*\* — Nextpower (NXT) dropped -6.53% to $83.48 in  
regular-session trading, down from the prior close of $89.31,  
extending Monday's -6.02% decline into a second straight session of  
losses. The selloff follows the November 16 Capital Markets Day, where  
management's FY2028 margin commentary implied another investment year,  
pushing operating leverage and profit conversion further out than  
investors had modeled.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-nextpower-inc-nxt-stock-down-6-53-today-39881/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-nextpower-inc-nxt-stock-down-6-53-today-39881/)  
  
\*\*5. Sasol (SSL)\*\* — SSL fell -6.11% to $13.07 from the prior close of  
$13.92, gapping down -6.82% in premarket and extending losses during  
Tuesday's regular session. The drop followed the pricing of US$750  
million of guaranteed senior unsecured convertible bonds announced  
before the Johannesburg open, a dilutive instrument that invites  
convertible-arbitrage hedging; Sasol was the JSE's worst performer,  
down -7.8% to R223.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-sasol-limited-ssl-stock-down-5-96-today-39891/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-sasol-limited-ssl-stock-down-5-96-today-39891/)  
  
\*\*6. Korea Electric Power (KEP)\*\* — KEP dropped -5.68%, sliding from  
the prior close of $9.69 on Nov 16 to $9.14 in regular-session trading  
on Nov 17, printing a fresh 52-week low. The decline extends the  
selloff triggered by the Nov 12 third-quarter report: operating profit  
fell -70.9% year over year and net income -78%, missing consensus  
badly, with the standalone parent posting an operating loss.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-korea-electric-power-corporation-kep-stock-down-5-78-today-39887/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-korea-electric-power-corporation-kep-stock-down-5-78-today-39887/)  
  
\*\*7. Futu (FUTU)\*\* — FUTU fell -5.36% to $86.69 from the prior close  
of $91.60, a -$4.91 decline, in regular-session trading mid-morning  
Tuesday, after trading roughly flat in premarket. The move tracked a  
broad China-ADR and technology risk-off: the Nasdaq closed -2.49% and  
the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -5.28% overnight on reports of  
tighter U.S. chip-related export controls, with Alibaba -4.9%, Tencent  
\-3.0% and...  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-futu-holdings-futu-stock-down-4-90-today-39894/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-futu-holdings-futu-stock-down-4-90-today-39894/)  
  
\*\*8. Circle Internet Group (CRCL)\*\* — CRCL dropped -5.2% to $54.65  
from Monday's close of $57.65, with the decline occurring during  
Tuesday's regular session after a roughly flat premarket. The driver  
was a fresh wave of crypto risk-off: Tuesday data showed total  
stablecoin supply down 5.3% over 30 days to about $284 billion, USDC  
included, the sharpest contraction since 2022 — directly hitting the  
reserve-income float Circle monetizes.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-circle-internet-group-crcl-stock-down-5-21-today-39884/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-circle-internet-group-crcl-stock-down-5-21-today-39884/)  
  
\*\*9. Cava Group (CAVA)\*\* — CAVA dropped -5.24% to $52.26 by late  
Tuesday morning, -$2.89 versus Monday's $55.15 close, with the decline  
occurring during the regular session after a slightly lower open. No  
company-specific news or filing explains the drop; the move extends a  
two-week slide from third-quarter results and mirrors a broad  
fast-casual selloff driven by rate-hike expectations, Treasury yields  
near 5% and soft traffic.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-cava-group-cava-stock-down-5-22-today-39896/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-cava-group-cava-stock-down-5-22-today-39896/)  
  
\*\*10. QXO (QXO)\*\* — QXO fell -5.00% to $11.41 from Monday's close of  
$12.01, with the decline occurring during Tuesday's regular trading  
session. The move extends the post-earnings de-rating from the  
November 12 third-quarter report: revenue of $4.90 billion beat  
estimates, but the GAAP loss widened to $(0.17) a share with only  
about $1 million of operating cash flow, prompting target cuts from  
Truist ($15), KeyBanc and DA...  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-qxo-inc-qxo-stock-down-5-16-today-39889/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-qxo-inc-qxo-stock-down-5-16-today-39889/)  
  
\*\*11. Navan (NAVN)\*\* — Navan, Inc. (NAVN) stock dropped -6.43% today,  
sliding from Monday's close of $25.98 to $24.31 during regular-session  
trading, a loss of -$1.67 per share. No verified news or fundamental  
catalyst found: no filings, guidance changes or fresh analyst actions  
preceded the slide, so it is likely profit-taking after Monday's +2.2%  
push stalled near the widely flagged 27.61 breakout level, with NAVN  
routinely...  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-navan-inc-navn-stock-down-6-00-today-39895/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-navan-inc-navn-stock-down-6-00-today-39895/)  
  
Overreaction or the start of something?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's (Nov 17) write-ups,  
using intraday or latest-close prices, not live quotes. Price targets  
are targets, not promises.
